definitions.gloss: to devote oneself; to dedicate oneself selflessly
definitions.explanation: To give oneself wholeheartedly to a cause, person, or purpose, often with self-sacrifice implied.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}のために{献身|けんしん}する。
examples.english: To devote oneself to one's family.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{地域|ちいき}の{医療|いりょう}に{献身|けんしん}してきた。
examples.english: She has devoted herself to community healthcare.

examples.japanese: {生涯|しょうがい}を{教育|きょういく}に{献身|けんしん}し、{多|おお}くの{学生|がくせい}を{育|そだ}てた{恩師|おんし}に{感謝|かんしゃ}している。
examples.english: I am grateful to the mentor who devoted their entire life to education and nurtured many students.

notes:
Composed of {献|けん} (to offer, dedicate) + {身|しん} (body, self). Implies selfless dedication, often with a sense of sacrifice. The noun form {献身|けんしん} is also common, often used as a modifier: {献身的|けんしんてき} (devoted, selfless).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {献身的|けんしんてき}な — devoted, selfless, dedicated
- {献身的|けんしんてき}な{介護|かいご} — devoted caregiving
- {献身的|けんしんてき}な{愛|あい} — selfless love
- {献身|けんしん}する{姿勢|しせい} — attitude of devotion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {尽|つ}くす — to serve devotedly, to exhaust oneself for someone; more everyday
- {捧|ささ}げる — to dedicate, to offer up; emphasizes giving something (life, time) to a cause
- {傾注|けいちゅう}する — to concentrate all one's effort; more intellectual, less self-sacrificing
